text.p: CLERKS USED TO STAFF SEXUAL ABUSE HOTLINE: COMMISSION
The New South Wales Education Department has admitted using untrained interviewers to receive complaints of sexual abuse by teachers.
The admission's been made at the Police Royal Commission, where the evidence continues to reveal new deficiencies in the Department's handling of such cases.
Education official Ros Coomber has told the Commission that clerks were used to staff a recent Hotline that's been flooded with complaints about teachers.
Ms Coomber has agreed under questioning that inexperienced interviewers could contaminate evidence of abuse.
She also agreed that her Unit is too small to cope with its task of handling all new and old cases alleging sexual abuse by teachers.
MAN SHOT DEAD BY SYDNEY SECURITY GUARD
A man has been shot dead by a security guard in a shopping centre car park at Cabramatta in Sydney's west.
Police say that just before two o'clock, two security guards approached a man and a woman who appeared to be acting suspiciously in the Woolworths car park.
The man is believed to have pulled out a screwdriver and lunged at one of the guards, who then fired two shots from his revolver.
Police say the security guards and the female companion of the dead man are being questioned.
KATTER MAY CROSS THE FLOOR ON SUGAR TARIFFS
Federal National Party backbencher, Bob Katter, says there is no way he can vote for the Government's plan to remove sugar tariffs.
Mr Katter says he will certainly be dividing the House on the issue.
The tariff cuts have been outlined by the Prime Minister as part of the Sugar Industry Review package.
Mr Katter says his Queensland seat of Kennedy includes around a third of the country's sugar producers.
Mr Katter says no responsible Government would expose it's primary producers to such a corrupt world market.
TOP GOVERNMENT JOB FOR MANSFIELD
The Prime Minister has confirmed he's appointed businessman Bob Mansfield as the Government's Major Projects Facilitator.
Mr Mansfield, who recently reviewed the role and responsibilities of the ABC, will be charged with ensuring speedy approval is given to big investment projects.
Mr Howard says Mr Mansfield, who's also the former head of Optus Communications and the Fairfax Newspaper Group, will spend about two to three days a week on the task.
The Prime Minister says he's delighted a businessman of Mr Mansfield's proven experience and status has agreed to perfrom this important new role.
CHILDREN'S TELEVISION FOUNDATION WORRIED ABOUT CABLE
The Australian Children's Television Foundation says cable television stations should be required to have local programming to stop them becoming pipelines for American culture.
The Australian Children's Television Foundation is celebrating 15 years of producing Australian shows, and is warning the globalisation of the industry is now its major challenge.
Director Patricia Edgar says cable outlets aimed at children could simply become pipelines for American programming and American profits.
VIC TO HOST RICHEST SURFING COMPETITION OF ALL-TIME
The richest single surfing event in the history of the sport will be held in Victoria next month.
115-thousand dollars or five thousand dollars a wave will be up for grabs at the Rip Curl Superskins to be held at Bell's Beach.
Three surfers enter the water for the first heat, the surfer who scores the best wave takes the money and stays in the water to compete with two new surfers.
The competition has attracted 23-local and international surfers including world champions Kelly Slater and Tom Carroll.
TYLER SHARMAN AND WATT TO RACE
In cycling...Lucy Tyler Sharman and Kathy Watt will finally race against each other in the 3000 metres individual pursuit at the National Cycling titles in Launceston on Thursday March 20.

The race is expected to again create contraversey with the Australian Cycling Federation allowing Lucy Tyler Sharman to use the "Superman" riding position which has been banned by the sports governing body.

By 0908 GMT, LIFFE June gilts were down 8/32 at 111-27/32. Dealers said there was little domestic news to give direction.

The UK monthly monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George takes place at 1100 GMT but dealers expect rates to stay unchanged at 6.0 percent.
"The strength of the pound is the key factor," said HSBC-Midland economist Jonathan Loynes.
"The Chancellor has stressed that he feels sterling's strength is very anti-inflationary and is affecting manufacturing," he said.

At the short end of the yield curve there were also slight losses. LIFFE June short sterling was down two basis points at 93.52, indicating three month cash rates of around 6.5 percent by the end of the second quarter.
A UK general election is expected on May 1 and analysts argue that whoever wins, interest rates will have to go up if the UK is to stay ahead of inflation.
